title: Authentication Basics
description: Add authentication to your GraphQL API.

data.text: Authentication verifies who the client is. In GraphQL, you typically authenticate once at the transport layer (HTTP or WebSocket) and reuse that identity throughout the request.
Hot Chocolate integrates with ASP.NET Core authentication. Configure JWT, cookies, or OAuth in Program.cs, and Hot Chocolate picks up the authenticated user automatically.

data.title: Configure JWT Auth

data.text: Inject `IHttpContextAccessor` or use the `[Service]` attribute to get the current `ClaimsPrincipal` inside resolvers.

data.title: Get Current User
data.content: Access the authenticated user in a resolver.

data.title: Stateless by Design
data.text: GraphQL is typically stateless. Authenticate with a token (JWT) on each request rather than relying on server-side sessions.

terms.definition: The process of verifying who a user is.
JSON Web Token — a compact, URL-safe token that carries claims about the user.
The .NET representation of the authenticated user and their claims.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Configure auth in ASP.NET Core, not GraphQL
Inject IHttpContextAccessor to get the current user
JWT is the standard token format for GraphQL APIs
data.takeaway: Next, we'll control access with authorization rules.
